USDCHF breaks below both hourly moving averages. Sellers eye 0.8339–0.8348.
body: The USDCHF has moved sharply lower after running into a ceiling near 0.8443 over the last four or so trading days. The buyers had several chances to extend the November rally through that level. Each time they fell short. Today, the sellers took the next step, pushing the price below the 100-hour moving average at 0.84143 and then the 200-hour moving average at 0.83992.

The pair is now trading near 0.8355, with the next test just below. A downward-sloping trend line meets a swing area between 0.8339 and 0.8348. That swing area has a number of reactions going back to October and again in November. With the price approaching it after a sharp move lower, it’s a place where buyers can lean against support and define their risk.

What would give the sellers more confidence? A move below 0.8339 that can stay below would open the door toward 0.83224, the 38.2% retracement of the November rally. Below that, 0.83121 is the next downside target. Get through that level and the 50% midpoint at 0.82851 comes into focus.

If the swing area holds and the price bounces, 0.83806 is the first upside hurdle. The 200-hour moving average at 0.83992 is the bigger barometer. As long as the price stays below it, the sellers keep the advantage. A move back above it would give buyers room to target the 100-hour moving average at 0.84143.

Fundamentally, SNB Vice Chairman Antoine Martin said over the weekend that inflation has accelerated since the central bank’s September meeting and that policymakers are watching for signs that higher costs are feeding into broader prices. Swiss inflation rose to 1.5% in October from 1.0% in September, more than expected. With the SNB’s policy rate still at 0%, that has put a possible December hike on traders’ radar. Those comments were already out heading into today’s session, but they give traders a reason to favor the franc as the Nvidia-led rally fades and demand for safe havens picks up.

The ceiling at 0.8443 showed where the buyers were having trouble. The breaks below the hourly moving averages showed that sellers were starting to take control. Now the question is whether they can keep that control through support. If the price breaks below 0.8339 and then stalls on a bounce back into the swing area, sellers have a level to lean against with close risk. If the price quickly gets back above 0.8348, that would be an early warning that the break is failing.

news.title: Consumer confidence shoots up after Democrats' midterm victories — though inflation worries persist
body: Consumers grew significantly more optimistic in November in the wake of the midterm elections, with a growing number of Americans now seeing improvement in the labor market and expecting inflation to cool.

The Conference Board survey released Tuesday showed improvement across the board, with the headline confidence index jumping to 103.3, up 11.4 points from October and much better than the Dow Jones consensus forecast for 92.2.

Confidence among Democrats and independent voters improved sharply, the Conference Board said, while confidence among Republican respondents fell slightly. Still, confidence among Republicans remained the highest among the three groups.

While respondents "continued to express frustration with high prices and rising costs," they also "cited hope for the general economy," said Fergus McCormick, the board's senior economist for global indicators.

The survey comes with the Federal Reserve continuing to try to bring down inflation, which has run above the central bank's 2% target for some 5½ years. The Fed is expected to raise its benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage point when it meets again in two weeks.

Despite the lingering worries about the cost of living — a centerpiece issue during the midterm — the survey's present situations and expectations indexes both posted strong gains. Inflation expectations for 12 months from now fell for the second straight month but remained high at 5.7%.

The survey's closely watched gap between jobs considered "plentiful" versus "hard to get" widened to 12.4 percentage points. The "plentiful" side rose to 30.8% from 26.2% while "hard to get" fell to 18.4%, down 3 percentage points.

The survey results are the second in the past week to show that Americans are growing more optimistic about the economy. The University of Michigan's November survey, released Friday, showed a 7.3% increase since October, with a similar partisan split.

news.title: Stock markets fall as Trump pivots from corporate meddling to fresh tariffs
body: Yesterday, he helped stock markets by intervening to reinstate Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Today, he's preparing to announce new tariffs on China and dozens of other countries and that's weighing on markets.

The WSJ was earlier out with the scoop, and it says that the US will hit China, the EU and many other countries with tariffs due to industrial subsidies. That said, it's not a surprise, the Trump administration has been working to reconstruct its tariff regime on firmer legal grounds since the Supreme Court struck down its original tariffs in February. Notably, on Friday Jamieson Greer told Bloomberg that the subsidy investigation would be done very soon and certainly before year end. There has been talk since August that the US was looking to add an additional 7.5% tariff on China.
These levels wouldn't be a surprise as they would return to the status quo from 2025.

The surpris is that the administration intends to target most imports rather than only industrial sectors with demonstrable excess capacity and it has provisions for tariffs to rise further if foreign countries don't change industrial policies.

Now this isn't another Liberation Day but it's an inflationary move into a time when the Fed is already hiking. The market is priced for 26 bps in December and 58 bps through March. That's come in since the latest market volatility but this threatens to make inflation more sticky and hit consumers with tariff headlines just as they're getting ready to go Christmas shopping.

news.title: Richmond Fed composite Index for November comes in higher at 3 versus -2 last month
body: The Richmond Fed composite Index for the month of November comes in stronger at 3 versus -2 last month.

Fifth District manufacturing activity improved modestly in November, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond. The composite index moved back above zero after two months at −2. New orders led the rebound, while shipments and employment also improved.

The outlook firmed as well. Expected shipments rose to 28 from 19, expected new orders to 27 from 22, and expected employment to 13 from 8. Input costs grew faster, while selling-price growth held steady. Firms expect both rates to ease over the next 12 months.

Current conditions improved across most of the Richmond Fed’s November manufacturing survey. Of the 17 current readings, including the headline index, 12 rose, three fell and two were unchanged. The composite index rose 5 points to +3 from −2, with all three of its components improving. New orders led the way, rising 10 points to +2, while employment rose 3 points and shipments rose 2 points. Order backlogs posted the biggest gain, up 15 points, though they remained negative at −6. Services spending rose 14 points but also stayed negative, while local business conditions climbed 12 points to +4.

The weaker spots were equipment and software spending, which slipped 1 point to −9, and the availability of needed skills, which fell 3 points to −10. Vendor lead times accounted for the third decline, though the lower reading signals that delivery times lengthened less broadly. On prices, input-cost growth picked up to 7.59% from 7.12%, while selling-price growth held at 5.27%. Finished goods inventories were also unchanged.

Expectations improved across much of the Richmond Fed’s November manufacturing survey. Of the 16 forward-looking readings, nine rose, five fell and two were unchanged. Expected shipments posted the biggest gain, rising 9 points to +28, while expected local business conditions climbed 8 points to +15. The outlook for new orders and employment also firmed, with both indexes up 5 points to +27 and +13, respectively. The expected availability of needed skills improved by 1 point but remained negative at −6.

Capital spending was the clearest weak spot, with the expectations index falling 5 points to −1 from +4 despite the stronger outlook for orders and shipments. Expected finished goods inventories fell 6 points to −3, and the wages index eased 5 points to +44. Firms also lowered their 12-month growth expectations for both prices paid, to 5.06% from 5.32%, and prices received, to 3.82% from 4.30%. Expectations for order backlogs and raw materials inventories were unchanged. The inflation guidance is good news.

The move back above zero is a modest positive for manufacturing, with new orders the component to watch for follow-through. Firmer demand and faster input-cost growth could lend some support to the US dollar and Treasury yields. Steady selling-price growth and expectations for easing price pressures limit what one regional survey is likely to change for the Fed.

The Richmond Fed’s monthly survey tracks shipments, new orders and employment at manufacturers in the Fifth Federal Reserve District. The seasonally adjusted composite is a diffusion index. A positive reading means improvement was more widespread than deterioration, and traders use it as an early regional read on factory demand and hiring.

news.title: Morning Kickstart. Nvidia slips after Monday’s surge. Nasdaq 100 futures fall 450 points. USD mostly lower
body: Nvidia shares are down 4.9% premarket after surging 31.48% on Monday, when Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO. The buying spread well beyond Nvidia yesterday, with the Nasdaq 100 gaining 6.86%. This morning, U.S. futures are lower across the board, with the Nasdaq 100 leading the decline. Monday’s InvestingLive market wrap. images.investinglive.com

Goldman Sachs’ technology, media and telecom desk said Huang’s return lifted sentiment and removed a major source of uncertainty for Nvidia. Bearish positioning also gave Monday’s rally room to run as shorts covered and underweight investors chased the move. The question now is whether buyers will defend the pullback. The cost of financing the AI buildout and whether the returns justify the spending are still in play. investing.com

Markets are pricing in a quarter-point hike at the December 8–9 meeting. The Fed raised rates by 25 basis points in September and held the target range at 3.75%–4.00% in October. The October minutes showed that almost all participants expected further tightening would likely be appropriate, and a couple were open to a move larger than 25 basis points at the next meeting if inflation data disappointed. Fed Governor Christopher Waller has also signaled he could support a half-point hike. For AI companies that need to raise or refinance debt, the path of rates beyond December matters too.

New York Fed President John Williams pointed to fading tariff effects, slower housing-services inflation and well-anchored inflation expectations on Monday. He expects inflation to slow to just above 2% in 2027. He also said inflation is still too high, flagged uncertainty around elevated energy prices and kept the pace of further tightening tied to the incoming data. FEDERAL RESERVE BANK of NEW YORK

The dollar is down against six of the seven majors in the morning snapshot. It is weakest against the euro, with EURUSD up 0.50% to 1.0956, followed by the pound, with GBPUSD up 0.41% to 1.3085. The yen is the exception. USDJPY is up 0.09% to 159.15. The dollar is also lower against the Swiss franc, Canadian dollar, Australian dollar and New Zealand dollar.

EURUSD is just 3 pips from its session high, and GBPUSD is 10 pips from its high. Those are the first upside tests heading into the U.S. data. USDJPY is near the middle of its range, with roughly 40 pips to either end.
Yields are lower alongside equity futures this morning. The 10-year is back below 4.90%.

January WTI crude is little changed at $80.08, down $0.09 after trading between $79.07 and $80.61. Gold is up 0.24% to $3,643.49, while silver is down 1.32% to $42.57. Copper is down 3.39% to $5.4430, and Bitcoin is down 1.13% to $60,519.

Copper traded to the lows level since March and is now down on the year and has corrected 22% from the high reached on September 23rd. The next target is the low from March at 5.246.Below that and the 50% midpoint from the start of the trend move higher back in July 2022 would be the target at 5.03. Lower copper prices is good for inflationary trends but sometime the price remains sticky to coming down after rising.

Crude oil prices are also -24% from the high reached at the end of October and -32% from the high from March 2026, but still above start of the year price near $57.60. The price is back below the 100 and 200 day MA nare $88.50. Stay below keeps the seller more in control. Targets at $76.53 and below that at the August low at $74.24. The July low at $67.28 was near the price just before the start of the US/Iran war on February 28.

Consumer confidence is the release I’ll be watching this morning. With December already priced for a hike, I’ll look to the 2-year yield for a read on whether the data are changing expectations for what comes after December. The bigger inflation test comes Wednesday at 8:30 a.m. ET, when October PCE and the second estimate of third-quarter GDP are due. U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA)

In the morning video above, I take a look at the three major currency pairs—EURUSD, USDJPY and GBPUSD—from a technical perspective. For each pair, I outline the bias, the risk-defining levels and the targets that would give either the buyers or sellers more control.

news.title: Zcash's Nvidia-induced rally fades quickly as hawkish Fed and geopolitical risks keep the market under pressure
body: Zcash spiked to the upside yesterday alongside other cryptocurrencies, as the news surrounding the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia’s CEO triggered a strong rally in equity markets and helped improve the risk sentiment.

However, the improvement in sentiment didn't really change the bigger picture, which remains challenging for the crypto market. In fact, the gains were quickly faded as the market continues to focus on the hawkish Fed and the deteriorating macro backdrop.

The Fed is still going to raise rates, and the extent of the tightening will depend on incoming economic data and stock market conditions. Meanwhile, the US-Iran stalemate remains unresolved, with Trump continuing to signal the possibility of renewed military action if negotiations fail.
While Zcash own fundamentals and developments in the privacy-focused crypto sector remain positive, the macro backdrop remains the dominant driver.

Looking ahead, the bearish trend in Zcash will likely persist as long as the macro conditions remain unchanged. A more sustained recovery will likely require a dovish shift in Fed stance or meaningful progress towards ending the Iran conflict.

On the daily chart, we can see that Zcash bounced from the support zone around the 680.00 level. If the price pulls back into the support again, we can expect the buyers to step in, with a defined risk below the support, to position for a rally into the downward trendline. The sellers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking lower to increase the bearish bets into the 500.00 level next.

On the 4 hour chart, we have a resistance zone around the 980.00 level. If the price gets there, we can expect the sellers to step in around the resistance, with a defined risk above it, to keep targeting new lows. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking higher to increase the bullish bets into the downward trendline.

On the 1 hour chart, there’s not much we can add here as the price action might remain choppy between the two major zones. The buyers will have a better risk to reward setup around the support, while the sellers will need a break to open the door for new lows. The red lines define the average daily range for today.
Today we get the US Consumer Confidence report. Tomorrow, we have the US Core PCE price index and the latest US Jobless Claims figures.
